name: Warm Blackish Brown
lede: Warm Blackish Brown is a near-black, slightly reddish brown, built from modifier grammar (warm + blackish) over the base color [[brown]], and filed by Ridgway in 1912.

sections.title: A modifier name, not a story
sections.body:
The name is built the way our data groups modifier colors: "warm" and "blackish" stack onto the base word [[brown]], rather than naming a plant, mineral or person [1]. Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* carries it on plate XXXIX, hue 1′′′, tone m, and the ISCC-NBS system filed it in 1955 in block 20, dark grayish red [2]. Its nearest listed neighbor there is [[bone-brown|Bone Brown]] [2].

Its closest look-alikes by measured color are [[starling|Starling]] and Bone Brown, both almost the same color, followed by a Greyish Umber pair and [[umber|Umber]] a little further out [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds this color in 1,138 of them, 4.79 percent, as photographed, more common than 86 percent of our named colors [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a mid-tone, in 40 percent of its appearances, a reading based on lightness rank within each canvas that varnish cannot fake [3]. It peaks in paintings from the 1100s, 2.4 times the expected rate for that century [3].

Its most devoted painter is Vilhelm Hammershøi, present in 13 of the 50 Hammershøi works in our archive, about 3.0 times the baseline for the museums those works come from [3]. The earliest match is a 960 panel attributed to Juran, 952 years before Ridgway's 1912 record; our archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first, and an aged, varnished photograph's color match is not proof of a painter's actual pigment [3].
